title: Urea Fertilizer 46 0 0: Uses, Timing, Losses and Price
metaTitle: Urea Fertilizer 46 0 0: Uses, Timing and Price Today
metaDescription: Urea fertilizer is 46 0 0, the richest nitrogen fertilizer in the store. Learn when to apply it on palay and mais, how to stop losses, and what a bag costs.
excerpt: Urea fertilizer is the white abono sold in 50 kg bags marked 46 0 0. It carries 46 percent nitrogen, the most of any common solid fertilizer. That makes it the main nitrogen source for palay and mais in the Philippines. Below, you will see what it does, when to apply it, how to stop losses and what a bag costs.

blocks.text:
Fertilizer in Tagalog is abono or pataba, and most farmers simply call this one urea. The agri supply sells two kinds. Prilled urea comes as small round beads, and granular urea as bigger, harder grains. Both are 46 0 0 fertilizer, and the Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority (FPA) tracks the price of each weekly. Our list of [farm words in Tagalog](/blog/farm-words-in-tagalog) covers the other names you will hear.

Urea is cheap per kilo of nitrogen, but it is easy to waste. If it goes on at the wrong stage or sits on wet ground, part of it never reaches the plant.
What urea fertilizer is and what 46 0 0 means

Every fertilizer bag shows three numbers called the grade. They give the percent of nitrogen (N), phosphate (P2O5) and potash (K2O), in that order. So 46 0 0 means 46 percent nitrogen and no phosphorus or potassium.

One 50 kg bag of urea holds 23 kg of nitrogen, since 50 times 0.46 is 23. Ammonium sulfate, the [21 0 0 fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), gives only 10.5 kg per bag but adds sulfur. For phosphorus and potassium, pair urea with [complete fertilizer 14 14 14](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14) or [16 20 0](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer).
What nitrogen fertilizer does for palay and mais

The IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank calls nitrogen the most limiting element in almost all soils. The PalayCheck guide of PhilRice lists what it does in rice. It adds plant height, tillers and leaf size, and more panicles per hill and spikelets per panicle. Corn also needs it for its leaves, stalk and ears.

Too much is also a problem. PhilRice warns that excess nitrogen at panicle initiation and flowering invites lodging and [pests](/pests/rice-insects). It also raises the share of unfilled grains and wastes money. So a good plan splits urea into doses instead of putting it all on at once.
Signs your crop is short of nitrogen

items: Older leaves turn yellowish green first, then the whole plant
Plants stay short, with few tillers
Fewer panicles and fewer grains per panicle at harvest
On a leaf color chart, 6 or more of 10 leaves read below 4 in transplanted rice, or below 3.5 in direct seeded rice

blocks.text: When to apply urea fertilizer on rice

The PalayCheck system ties nitrogen to growth stages, not to a fixed date. Without a leaf color chart, Key Check 5 splits nitrogen by variety maturity, as in the table below. In PhilRice bag plans, the first dose usually comes from complete fertilizer or 16 20 0. Those also carry phosphorus and potassium, and urea supplies the later doses.

blocks.caption: Nitrogen timing for palay from PhilRice PalayCheck Key Check 5, for farms without a leaf color chart
rows: 5 to 7 days before or after panicle initiation

blocks.text:
DAT means days after transplanting. DAS means days after sowing, for direct seeded rice. If you own a leaf color chart, read it every 7 days from 14 DAT, or 21 DAS, until early flowering. Apply nitrogen only when the leaves call for it.

A DA, PhilRice and IRRI quick guide for Nueva Ecija gives windows for the top dressing fertilizer in the wet season. Active tillering comes at 23 to 27 DAT for early varieties and 28 to 32 DAT for medium ones. Panicle initiation follows at 33 to 37 DAT and 43 to 47 DAT for the same groups. Treat these as a guide, since fields differ. The full season plan is on our [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) page.
When to apply urea fertilizer on corn

At planting, the DA Region 2 corn guide puts all the phosphorus and potassium and half the nitrogen in the furrow. It goes in a band about 5 cm beside and 5 cm below the seed. The rest of the nitrogen goes on as a side dress 21 to 30 days after planting, during hilling up. That second dose is where urea fits best.

Hilling up covers the urea with soil right away, which also cuts losses. For a dry season crop, the guide says to apply all the fertilizer at planting while the soil is still moist. Read more in our guide to [pagtatanim ng mais](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).
Why urea fertilizer escapes into the air, and how to stop it

Once urea touches moist soil, an enzyme called urease turns it into ammonium within about two days. The water around each granule turns alkaline. Part of the ammonium then changes into ammonia gas and floats away. Agronomists call this loss volatilization.

The loss is worst when urea sits on a wet soil surface or goes straight into floodwater. IRRI also flags calcareous and alkaline soils as high risk. So the aim is simple: get the urea into the soil, or into the plant, fast.

items: Mix the basal dose into the mud during the last harrowing, as IRRI advises
On corn, cover the side dress with soil when you hill up
Split nitrogen into two or three doses by growth stage, as PalayCheck recommends
Spread evenly so no corner of the paddy gets a double dose
Keep bunds and outlets closed after top dressing so the dissolved fertilizer stays in your field
On upland crops, apply just before a light rain or an irrigation that carries the urea into the soil

blocks.title: Check the price for your own region
blocks.text: The FPA weekly price list gives the average dealer price per region and per province. Look it up before you buy, so you know if a quote from your dealer is fair.
Urea fertilizer price in the Philippines

Prices move every week, so check before you buy. The FPA dealer survey for September 14 to 18, 2026 gives the national weighted averages. Prilled urea stood at **PHP 2,320.69** per 50 kg bag and granular urea at **PHP 2,322.28**. By region, prilled urea ran from PHP 2,156.05 in the Cordillera to PHP 2,677.79 in Region X.

In the week of January 5 to 9, 2026, prilled urea averaged PHP 1,694.25. That is about PHP 626 more per bag in eight months. The PSA also publishes a monthly update on fertilizer prices.

blocks.caption: National average dealer prices per 50 kg bag from the FPA weekly survey. Prices change every week.

blocks.text: Compare the price per kilo of nitrogen

Divide the bag price by the kilos of nutrient inside. At the September 2026 averages, urea gives nitrogen at about PHP 100.90 per kg. Ammonium sulfate gives it at about PHP 115.58 per kg. But each ammonium sulfate bag also brings 12 kg of sulfur, useful on soils that lack it.
Fertilizer calculation: how many bags of urea you need

items.title: Know your nitrogen target
items.text: Start from a soil test, the Rice Crop Manager, MOET or your technician. As a general guide only, the modified general recommendation of PhilRice lists 97 kg of nitrogen per hectare for irrigated lowland rice in the wet season and 139 kg in the dry season. Your own target may differ.

items.title: Subtract the nitrogen from other fertilizers
items.text: Two bags of 14 14 14 at basal give 14 kg of nitrogen. For a 97 kg target, that leaves 83 kg for urea.

items.title: Divide by 0.46
items.text: 83 divided by 0.46 is about 180 kg of urea. At 50 kg per bag, that is 3.6 bags for one hectare.

items.title: Scale it to your lot
items.text: For a 0.75 hectare lot, multiply by 0.75 to get about 135 kg, or 2.7 bags. Then split it by stage as PalayCheck shows.

blocks.text: Our [fertilizer calculation](/blog/fertilizer-calculation) guide does phosphorus and potassium the same way. For broadcasting, banding and side dressing, see [fertilizer application methods](/blog/fertilizer-application-methods).
Plan every urea fertilizer dose in anee.io

Each lot in anee.io keeps its own day zero. So the [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) dates every urea dose by DAT, DAS or DAP, and a lot planted late keeps its own timing. The [farm inventory](/features/farm-inventory-and-expenses) counts your urea in 50 kg bags. Tick a fertilizer task done and it takes those bags out of stock and adds their cost to your expense report.

Not sure how many bags your lot needs? Ask Anee, the [AI agricultural technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), in Tagalog or English. She reads your lot size, crop and stage, then works out a fertilizer plan to check against your soil test.

blocks.text: Questions farmers ask about urea fertilizer

items.q: What is the difference between urea and 46 0 0?
items.a: There is none. Urea is the fertilizer and 46 0 0 is its grade. That means 46 percent nitrogen, no phosphate and no potash.

items.q: How much nitrogen is in one bag of urea?
items.a: A 50 kg bag holds 23 kg of nitrogen. About 2.2 bags of ammonium sulfate give the same amount.

items.q: When should I apply urea as top dressing on palay?
items.a: Follow the growth stage. PalayCheck puts the later doses at mid tillering and around panicle initiation. For a variety of 110 days or less, the second dose goes on 5 to 7 days before panicle initiation.
Abono or pataba. Most farmers still call urea by its own name.

items.q: Is granular urea fertilizer better than prilled urea?
items.a: Both are 46 0 0 with the same nitrogen per bag. Granules are larger and harder than prills. Compare prices, since the September 2026 FPA averages for the two were almost equal.
